cards.a: GET VPN (Group Encrypted Transport VPN) provides any-to-any encryption over an MPLS or IP backbone without tunnel interfaces, using a shared GDOI group key so member routers encrypt directly with each other.

cards.q: What is the role of a Key Server (KS) in GET VPN?
cards.a: The Key Server manages and distributes group keys to members over GDOI; it sends the KEK and TEK so members can encrypt peer-to-peer without building tunnels.

cards.q: What do TEK and KEK stand for in GET VPN?
cards.a: TEK is the Traffic Encryption Key used to encrypt data, and KEK is the Key Encryption Key that protects distribution of the TEK.

cards.q: What protocol and port does GET VPN use for key management?
cards.a: GET VPN uses GDOI (Group Domain of Interpretation) on UDP 848 for members to register with the key server and receive group keys.

cards.q: How does GET VPN differ from DMVPN?
cards.a: GET VPN uses no tunnel interfaces and a shared GDOI group key for direct any-to-any encryption, while DMVPN uses mGRE plus NHRP for spoke-to-spoke tunnels with hub control.

cards.q: Why does GET VPN avoid a hub bottleneck?
cards.a: After registering with the key server, members share a TEK and encrypt directly to each other, so no hub sits in the data path and traffic is not hair-pinned.

cards.q: What does COOP provide in GET VPN?
cards.a: COOP (Cooperative Key Server) provides redundant key servers for GET VPN high availability and continuous key distribution.

cards.q: Which commands verify GET VPN status?
cards.a: show crypto gdoi group, show crypto gdoi ks, show crypto gdoi member, show crypto ipsec sa, and debug crypto gdoi.

cards.q: A GET VPN member cannot register; what is a likely cause?
cards.a: GDOI traffic on UDP 848 is likely blocked or the key server is unreachable; check show crypto gdoi and reachability to the key server.

cards.q: What is the key GET VPN exam distinction from other VPN types?
cards.a: GET VPN uses a shared GDOI group key with no tunnel interfaces at all, so it encrypts natively and any-to-any over an MPLS/backbone, unlike DMVPN or crypto-map/VTI which build point-to-point tunnels.

cards.q: What is the GET VPN quick-review summary?
cards.a: GET VPN is group-key IPsec based on GDOI (UDP 848) with no tunnels, where members register at a Key Server, receive a TEK (data) and KEK (key), and encrypt directly any-to-any, best suited to MPLS or backbone networks with COOP redundancy.
